issues.summary: S2 prints '100 - 96.0 = 4.11' for the technology residual; the residual is 4.0 and the share 1.30%, not 1.34%, and the numeral 4.11% separately denotes aquaculture on a different base.
12.79% has no in-text derivation, no generating method, and wholly contains the 7.64% presented beside it as an independent quantity.
Corpus and supplements are repeatedly claimed as deposited, but no Data or Code Availability statement, repository, accession, DOI or licence exists anywhere.
The central result is a single-coder grading deposited at row level though the tested population is 62 items, with boilerplate grounds on rows 33-44 and no reliability threat named in Limitations.
No figure legend, caption, embed or filename reference exists for any of the five cited figures, leaving four load-bearing figure claims uncheckable.
The nominal-versus-effective weight objection is conceded in 5.5 but absent from abstract and conclusion, and the escape sentence names what survives without naming what does not.
The only compiled Indonesian instance is reclassified out of the evidence base at the point where it disconfirms the provenance claim.
Corpus extraction is 'purposive' with no inclusion, boundary or stopping rule, and the reconstruction flag carried by 17 records is never defined.
The renormalisation test bounds closure, not the loadings-versus-contributions ambiguity it is offered against, and 3.5 calls the ambiguity singular when S4.1 supplies a second.
13.70% cannot be recomputed from the deposit: all four social component rows leave the printed-input cell blank.
CONTESTED DENOMINATOR is flagged once in Section 4 though Methods scopes it to all derived figures, and structure-dependence is flagged at some dependent figures and not others.
The 1.07 ratio between two indicative figures differing by 0.91 percentage points cannot bear the comparability argument the abstract and introduction rest on it.
No keywords, Highlights, funding statement, competing-interests declaration, CRediT statement or acknowledgements; submission-blocking at Marine Policy.
assemble.sh's MAIN array omits drafts/references.md, so the assembled manuscript contains no reference list.
The authors' own superseded mapping is corrected in prose but has no reference-list entry, and the abstract does not disclose the correction as self-correction.
The Discussion answers a character-of-contribution question rather than the Introduction's production-capacity question, and restates none of the four load quantities.

Original computation and the pillar-locus decision sit inside the background section, the findings preview lands before 1,070 further words of gap-building, and four contributions are previewed as three.
A bolded design recommendation and several evaluative or mechanism claims leak into Results from the Discussion.

The Wuwung institutional-constraint concession is not permitted to alter the loose-coupling recommendation, and an absence of contrary sources is converted into support without restating the search bound.
The competing position that secondary compilation plus uncertainty analysis suffices for a policy composite is never engaged, leaving the paper's central premise under-tested.
The falsification condition's cost arm is unfalsifiable because the paper declines to estimate the cost it names as the binding constraint.
Two of four conclusion paragraphs restate the abstract and introduction in near-identical clause order rather than synthesising.
The abstract's central contribution is phrased as a method rather than a result, and its closing generalisation exceeds the Discussion's own disclaimer, inverting the proportionality chain.
The closing claim generalises one 2,980.84 ha pilot to a 38-province annual obligation despite naming that pilot's own method limits two paragraphs earlier.
13.70% is rendered 13.7% at five points in Results; same value, but two-decimal precision is unwarranted given a documented 0.33 pp branch.
2,980.84 ha is carried at 0.01-ha precision in the paragraph showing it fails to reconcile by 32.35 ha, and the district-size comparison is unsourced.
Forty-eight inline bracketed evidential flags sit in finished main-text prose; most journals will require footnotes or a caveat table.
CONTESTED DENOMINATOR is given two different definitions in the same section.
Abstract is 282 words, about 13% over Marine Policy's conventional 250-word guidance.
The abstract opens at subfield breadth with five unglossed specialist terms; major under Nature's accessibility standard, minor for Marine Policy's readership.
Six subheadings exceed 40 characters; Nature-only, no Marine Policy limit.
S1 cites 'Section 7' and 'Section 8.5' from the dead v1 numbering; the only two stale cross-references in the manuscript.
The English gloss's provenance is unstated and no software, script or spreadsheet is named anywhere.
The 6.26 ha figure makes its first main-text appearance in the Discussion; its derivation is in S5.2 but not in Section 4.
Indicator 27 is returned to at L569 after being settled at L449-467.
The tables 18-19 citation omits the [pdf N] locator used at every other citation.
The loose-coupling failure-isolation property is asserted of an arrangement never instantiated and is not ASSUMPTION-flagged.
The objection vitiating the headline quantities sits after the policy recommendation it undercuts.
The second follow-on study is close to a generic call for guidance, and the cost trade-off is justified but not owned as a limitation.
The novelty claim would be strengthened by naming the adjacent class of national statistical quality-assurance production audits.
The three quantitative findings are listed without signalling which is central, and the caveat sentence interrupts the widening close.
